source.title: An Interpretable Neuron Embedding for Static Knowledge Distillation
source.authors: Wei Han; Yangqiming Wang; C. Böhm; Jun-Ming Shao

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The study treats individual neurons as units for semantic embedding and uses their semantic relations as static knowledge, but it does not test any of the listed claim versions or the audit's job-count estimates.
record.gate_note: The study assumes neuron activations can be represented by semantic vectors and reports qualitative and quantitative results about that representation. It does not report how many neurons have one or multiple jobs, test explanation fidelity on held-out activations, compare interpretability shares across models or tools, or build attribution graphs. The CIFAR-100 distillation accuracy results concern downstream performance, not the claim's neuron-interpretability measures, so they are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study learns semantic vectors for ResNet18 neurons and uses them for knowledge distillation. It reports no share of neurons with one or several jobs and no held-out explanation scoring. It does not touch InceptionV1, tool or architecture effects, or neuron-based attribution graphs. Its only links to the claim are passing: a remark that some pre-trained neurons 'show polysemy', and a cited NetDissect result that a third of neurons lack specific meaning. Neither is the study's own test of any version. The record's T4/'assumes' label does not fit, because the method does not rely on neurons being monosemantic.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that neuron semantic vectors describe neuron semantics well, based on qualitative visualizations and a KL comparison to annotation-derived vectors. They add that the resulting static knowledge gives distillation results comparable to or better than existing relation-based methods on CIFAR-100.
record.recipe_differences: The study learns semantic vectors by aligning pairwise activation and vector similarities; it does not use the audit or explanation-testing procedures in the claim's sources.

fits_no_version.finding: In a pre-trained ResNet18, similarity between learned semantic vectors corresponds qualitatively to similarity between activation maps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation-similarity embeddings of neurons capture relations among neuron activation patterns.

fits_no_version.finding: Unsupervised neuron semantic vectors move toward NetDissect IoU-based target vectors over training, as measured by falling KL divergence (figure only).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation-similarity neuron embeddings partly recover annotation-based neuron semantics.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding the vectors of two neurons with simple semantics points to neurons with complex, sometimes polysemous, semantics. This is shown by qualitative examples only.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Some polysemous-looking neurons can be approximated as combinations of simpler neurons in embedding space.

record.problems: Neuron-semantic results are qualitative or shown as a plot without exact values in the text; the paper reports no uncertainty for these results and does not validate the interpretation claims on held-out activations.
record.rows_left_out: CIFAR-100 knowledge-distillation accuracy comparisons in Table 1 are downstream task results, not measurements of the neuron-interpretability claim.

untested.parts: No audit of Qwen3-32B neuron poles or job counts.
No cross-model or cross-scale interpretability shares; only one vision model is analysed.
No analysis of InceptionV1 cat-and-car neurons, pose, or recursive generalization.
No comparison of interpretable-neuron shares across tools, architectures or regularization.
No attribution graphs or circuit explanations from neurons.
No test of activating-example explanations against held-out firing.
No simulation-based scoring of neuron explanations.

record.verdict_notes: Changed the tranche from T4 to T6 and the relation from 'assumes' to 'discusses'. The method needs no assumption that neurons are monosemantic. The NetDissect figure (a third of neurons lack specific semantics) is a cited result, not this study's own, so it is correctly not a row. The CIFAR-100 distillation accuracies in Table 1 are correctly left out.

versions.untested_parts: No audit of Qwen3-32B or other model's neuron poles; no counts of single-job, two-job, or not-understood poles.
No comparison of interpretability shares across models, architectures, or scales.
No analysis of InceptionV1 cat-and-car neurons, pose, or recursive generalization.
No comparison of interpretability shares across tools, architectures, or regularization settings, and no estimate for InceptionV1-sized models.
No attribution graphs or test of behavioral reconstruction using a model's own neurons.
No test of explanations against activations they were not written from.
No automated scoring of neuron explanations on new text.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Compared activation-map similarity of neurons with similarity of their learned semantic vectors; visualized the three most similar neurons for selected top-layer neurons.
rows.measure: Qualitative correspondence between semantic-vector similarity and activation-map similarity across images
rows.value: The paper reports that neurons with similar semantic vectors reflect similar activation, including in images with different semantics.
rows.note: This is evidence about the learned representation's correspondence to activations, not a count of neurons with one main job.
rows.check: Link to none is correct. The row measures the method's own representation fidelity, shown qualitatively, not neuron interpretability shares.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Measured KL divergence between optimized semantic vectors and target vectors constructed from Broden neuron responses during embedding training.
rows.measure: KL divergence to manually annotated semantic vectors
rows.baseline: Randomly initialized semantic vectors; exact value not stated
rows.value: figure only; the text says the KL-divergence curve decreases continuously during training
rows.note: The paper also shows an optimized-for-KL upper bound, but gives no exact plotted values in the text.
rows.check: Link to none is correct. KL divergence to NetDissect-derived IoU vectors is figure-only. It evaluates the study's own embedding method against random and upper-bound vectors, not the claim.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Added pairs of neuron semantic vectors and compared the combined vectors with vectors in the original semantic space.
rows.measure: Qualitative examples of complementary combinations and neurons described as showing polysemy
rows.value: The paper reports that combinations of neurons with simple semantics can correspond to neurons with more complex semantics; selected target neurons are described as showing polysemy.
rows.note: Qualitative examples only; this does not estimate the prevalence of polysemantic neurons or test the specified classic examples.
rows.check: Link to none is correct. The polysemy remark covers a few selected target neurons and gives no prevalence estimate, so it cannot bear on V1, V2 or V4.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
